sources.text: This review looks at how people learn from lectures and what teachers can change. Attention in lectures tends to drift after about ten minutes, and students who take notes by hand recall the main ideas better than students who type verbatim transcripts. The studies were carried out in universities in several countries between 2005 and 2020. Working memory holds only a handful of items at once, so instruction that overloads it leaves learners unable to connect new facts with what they already know. None of the findings here is final, and each rests on samples that are small.
